pdlmi Constructor

Documents/pdlmi/constructor
DirectLPólyaL.applyPolya(p)PutinarL.applyPutinar()Full BoxL.applyFullBoxPreorder()

Purpose

Section titled “Purpose”

Build a pdlmi object from a pdvar residual expression and one supported relation.

Syntax

Section titled “Syntax”

Description

Section titled “Description”

Direct coefficient-wise assembly is the default. For <= and >=, one scan of every original coefficient selects semidefinite mode only when all are square Hermitian (numeric tolerance 1e-10 inclusive); otherwise the entire inequality is entry-wise and warns once with pdlmi:ElementwiseInequality. For ==, direct column-major coefficient equality accepts rectangular and non-Hermitian residuals. UsePolya selects exact degree elevation before coefficient constraints. In one parameter, UsePutinar and UseFullBoxPreorder select the same parity-specific Markov–Lukács interval form. In two or more parameters, UsePutinar selects one unweighted Gram term plus one αs(1−αs)\alpha_s(1-\alpha_s)αs​(1−αs​)-weighted term per axis, while UseFullBoxPreorder selects a term for every generator-subset product. All three opt-in selections are mutually exclusive.

Use the direct default first. Choose Pólya when you want one exact degree elevation followed by the same coefficient test. In one parameter the two Gram selectors are equivalent. In two or more parameters, choose full box for every generator-subset product or Putinar for the unweighted term plus the separate axis generators. For derivations and the difference between representation degree and certificate order, see SOS Certificates On A Hypercube.

Arguments And Options

Section titled “Arguments And Options”
InputDescription
exprpdvar residual expression, such as P, V-Q, or diffP + P*A + A'*P.
relation"<=", ">=", or "==".
UsePolyaLogical option. Default false. The bare flag "UsePolya" enables Pólya assembly with increment one.
PolyaDegreeFinite nonnegative integer scalar. Default 0. Supplying it without UsePolya enables Pólya and warns pdlmi:ImplicitUsePolya.
UseFullBoxPreorderLogical scalar. Default false. The bare flag and explicit true select full-box assembly at the minimum admissible order.
FullBoxOrderFinite nonnegative integer scalar. This is an absolute order, not a degree increment. Supplying it alone enables full-box assembly without a warning.
UsePutinarLogical scalar. Default false. The bare flag and explicit true select Putinar box assembly at the minimum admissible order.
PutinarOrderFinite nonnegative integer scalar. This is an absolute order, not a degree increment. Supplying it alone enables Putinar assembly without a warning.

When full-box assembly is active, the minimum order is floor(expr.Degree/2) for one parameter and ceil(expr.Degree/2) for two or more parameters. Explicitly pairing UseFullBoxPreorder=false with FullBoxOrder=r keeps direct assembly active while retaining r as inspectable metadata. This combination is valid and is not a relaxation conflict.

When Putinar assembly is active, the minimum and default order are floor(expr.Degree/2) in one parameter and ceil(expr.Degree/2) in two or more parameters. Unlike the full-box metadata form, explicitly pairing UsePutinar=false with any supplied PutinarOrder is rejected. Enabling more than one of Pólya, Putinar, and full-box assembly is also rejected.

Returned Object

Section titled “Returned Object”

C is a pdlmi object with private-set, inspectable Constraints, Residual, Relation, UsePolya, PolyaDegree, UseFullBoxPreorder, FullBoxOrder, UsePutinar, and PutinarOrder properties. Constraints contains direct coefficient inequalities, Pólya-elevated coefficient inequalities, or the PSD blocks and exact identities for the selected Gram mode.

Equality stores direct coefficient equalities only. A proven identity may have empty Constraints; inspect properties with dot access such as C.Relation, C.Residual, and C.Constraints.

Examples

Section titled “Examples”

Direct constructor form

Section titled “Direct constructor form”

The direct constructor is useful when code already has a residual expression and a relation string.

Comparison-overload form

Section titled “Comparison-overload form”

A scalar grid with one physical cell and degree 1 has two local Bernstein coefficients, so this direct constraint has two stored coefficient entries.

Pólya option forms

Section titled “Pólya option forms”

one uses an increment of one. two uses two, while implicit also uses two and emits pdlmi:ImplicitUsePolya. Pólya assembly rebuilds the stored residual at the selected degree, constraining every elevated coefficient and active rate-vertex row. It does not mutate the input expression or source pdlmi: one = direct.applyPolya() leaves direct.UsePolya false and returns one.UsePolya true. Reapplying another selector likewise rebuilds a new object from Residual; it never accumulates certificate constraints in the existing object.

Full-box option forms

Section titled “Full-box option forms”

FullBoxOrder alone selects full-box assembly without a warning. The final form deliberately suppresses that implicit selection: it records order two, but its three constraints are the direct degree-two coefficient conditions.

Putinar option forms

Section titled “Putinar option forms”

PutinarOrder alone selects Putinar assembly without a warning. Name-value syntax and paired string/value syntax select the same implemented mode. Each object uses independent Gram blocks and exact coefficient identities; construction does not call a solver or add a positivity margin.

Validation And Errors

Section titled “Validation And Errors”
  • Nonsquare or non-Hermitian inequality coefficients select supported entry-wise mode and warn once with pdlmi:ElementwiseInequality.
  • Rectangular and non-Hermitian equality coefficients are supported.
  • A non-pdvar residual raises pdlmi:InvalidExpression; an unsupported relation raises pdlmi:InvalidRelation.
  • Nonlogical selectors raise pdlmi:InvalidUsePolya, pdlmi:InvalidUseFullBoxPreorder, or pdlmi:InvalidUsePutinar.
  • Invalid Pólya increments, full-box orders, or Putinar orders raise pdlmi:InvalidPolyaDegree, pdlmi:InvalidFullBoxOrder, or pdlmi:InvalidPutinarOrder.
  • When a Gram mode is enabled, a valid integer below its applicable minimum raises pdlmi:FullBoxOrderTooLow or pdlmi:PutinarOrderTooLow.
  • UsePolya=false with a positive PolyaDegree raises pdlmi:ConflictingPolyaOptions.
  • UsePutinar=false with an explicit PutinarOrder raises pdlmi:ConflictingPutinarOptions, even when the order is zero.
  • Enabling more than one of Pólya, Putinar, and full-box assembly raises pdlmi:ConflictingRelaxations.
  • Malformed, duplicate, or unknown options raise pdlmi:InvalidOptions, pdlmi:DuplicateOption, or pdlmi:UnknownOption.
  • Any Pólya, Putinar, or Full Box option on relation "==" raises pdlmi:UnsupportedEqualityCertificate.

In one parameter, Putinar and full-box assembly share the exact parity-specific Markov–Lukács form. In two or more parameters, Putinar is limited to the local hypercube generators αs(1−αs)\alpha_s(1-\alpha_s)αs​(1−αs​) and full-box assembly uses every generator-subset product. Neither is a general-domain or general-generator interface or an automatic hierarchy selector. No assembly mode adds an implicit positivity margin or calls a solver.
